record_notes.DCP-LETT-1363: Ramsgate, October 18–22, 1850 from itinerary. Missing Lankester letter travelled by wrong/incomplete address and followed Darwin, exact receipt unknown. Return in about ten days and manuscript review promised; actual October 22 departure is later itinerary evidence, not current completion. No incoming letter is preserved in1361: that record substitutes October7 council minute. Missing delivered prompt cannot be reconstructed from institutional instruction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1364: October27, supplied1850. Manuscript reviewed and could be ready in a fortnight, but proofs needed for cross-references, not already press-ready with finished engravings. Requests7–10plates, roughly half coloured, GB Sowerby junior as engraver, and possible specimen plate/estimate. Current work delays start3–4weeks and authorization still needed. Three-part plan is current, later abandoned. Later eight-plate decision and1851revision/ten final plates must not rewrite proposal.1366A records council consideration of this letter, but does not reproduce subsequent secretary letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1367: November7, supplied1850. Skeleton plates posted yesterday; four finished drawings already made. Requests their preservation/return and estimate, does not say final engraved plates exist. Eight-plate ceiling conditional on council, colour not yet answered. Type options produce estimates192/150/175pages, not final400-page outcome. Second systematic part expected twice size;1851part or1852whole desired, not agreed production schedule. Apparatus November18resolution and1854volume later.1366A is council minute directing missing secretary request, not actual incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1374: December5, supplied1850. Missing note now establishes eight plates with two coloured. Explicitly corrects mistaken belief Sowerby had made engraved plates: only drawings. Return of skeletons/drawings requested, not received. Publication within1851 queried, intended sequencing after fossil part not a completed press stage. Footnote distinguishes volume nominal1851 from actual1852appearance; neither is current knowledge of definite schedule.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1157: February14, supplied1848 from Admiralty commission. Requests Phillips reference and more cases/details of boulders above parent rock; current asserted true explanation remains Darwin hypothesis. Hopkins, Milne, Hitchcock and Glen Roy observations cited with own limited care. Heights and further observations queried, not later established numbers. Separate Admiralty suggestions sought. Printed1848paper in apparatus is later outcome, not missing Phillips answer or current final theory.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1162: March7, supplied1848. Missing earlier reference has been consulted, but Hopkins conglomerate case seems different. Stainmoor height, map location, route and angularity uncertain; does not yet possess later final500/1400/900-foot account. P5 asks whether highest slate boulders more worn, a distinct question from later conglomerate query. Apparatus infers non-answer because question persists in printed paper; absence of a reply is inference, not proof no communication. Criticism of Hopkins is historical voice.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1163: Sunday conjectured March12,1848. Full missing note received and Lardner reference immediately consulted/reread; earlier reading remembered, not first access now. Proposed coast-ice/subsidence explanation explicitly separates coast ice from icebergs and is hypothesis, not modern fact. Specific rounded-versus-angular upper conglomerate question still open; silence would be interpreted as inability to answer. March12 remains questioned, no exact receipt date. Later printed inference cannot supply missing incoming text.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1170: Friday April7 OR April14,1848, two discrete alternatives before April19meeting, not every intervening day. Oral De la Beche/other geologists objection depicts denudation explanation; preserved figure is a schematic of that alternative, not empirical measured section or Darwin endorsement. Wants Phillips quotable reason and geological inclination; no answer yet. Published paper later cites conclusive Phillips reasons, supporting later communication but not its surviving text or earlier availability. Expected criticism is author expectation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1109: Monday April12–May17,1847, inferred relative to1047. Carrier next Thursday and box planned; promised fortnight reading/return not receipt. Rarity only learned after request. June13log of first Transactions volume and August loan of broader set are separate. No Royle incoming offer survives.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1047: Friday April16–May21,1847, calendar/club bounds. Carrier left before note arrived yesterday, so earlier request was acted on before learning books unavailable. Cannot lend now due to cotton committee work; future loan months later acceptable. Offer of other breed sources received, Royle productive-resources book already known. New club is Philosophical Club of Royal Society, not initial Royal Society fellowship. Missing incoming note and invitation, no book receipt here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1108: August14, supplied1847. Renewed offer received, Thursday carrier pickup still planned and prior box already at Royle house. Philosophical Club candidacy, not new Royal Society fellowship; already fellow1839. Blacklock treatise requested if owned; no evidence actually received or read, notebook only to-be-read. Later August25reading-completion log does not make volumes available at letter outset.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1112: September1, supplied1847. Returns borrowed volumes and reports looking through them; found less variety information than expected, climate effects judged premature. August25log is independent earlier completion evidence in apparatus, not original letter wording. National/colonial praise is actual historical author voice, not editor interpretation or modern instruction. Exact initial delivery and Royle note text remain missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1054: January20, supplied1847. Interested in Studer letter published in Edinburgh journal, not a direct incoming personal letter. Sends own South America book and directs pages162–168, linking foliation/cleavage. Studer English ability unknown here. Publication date alone is insufficient earlier knowledge, but explicit present reading supports current familiarity.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1073: March21, supplied1847, recipient identified by addressed cover. Missing kind Studer letter read; own book dispatched through publisher, expected arrival not proved. Newly learns Studer English and prior coral discussion. Bulletin paper heard of and will consult, not read yet; Sharpe cleavage paper read with difficulty. Flow/stretching analogy extended as tentative theory. German book offer conditionally accepted if not large/expensive due to poor language proficiency; no receipt or full reading established.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1102: July4, supplied1847. Found missing Studer letter on return from Oxford after forwarding failed, thereby missed friend introduction. Has only heard pamphlet reached brother Park Street and expects to get it at week end; not own physical possession or reading. Pamphlet identity only possibly1844memoir in apparatus. Tour/introductions and Sharpe inquiry prospective. Personal health/language claims historical self-report; reads French easily but cannot speak it. No exact letter-arrival date.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1107: August13, supplied1847. Just received arrival note; supposes earlier July4reply reached Berne, not receipt proof. Visit versus Monday London meeting conditional, Saturday note/Sunday expected arrival planned. Raw MathML travel estimate is three quarters of an hour, not34hours. Sharpe already informed and De la Beche instructions received, but those incoming notes absent. Literal Ordnance Survey denotes Geological Survey according to apparatus; preserve wording and separate identification. Map loan offered, visit not proved completed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-415: Fresh complete context: Thursday May24,1838 inferred. Heard of Himalayan plant lecture, asks time/place and wants to attend, not already lecture knowledge. Later June1lecture/notebook report is later evidence. Previous-night Sedgwick/Greenough exchange reported. No later1847loan prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-473: Fresh complete context: Monday March18,1839 inferred from Tuesday lecture. Map sent in response to absent request, asks admission/time but attendance uncertain due to engagement. Later March20notebook entry separate from current intent. No1848boulder inquiry response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-578: Fresh complete surviving context: incomplete letter November1840. Encloses earthquake paper and now qualifies earlier theoretical confidence while retaining slow-elevation argument. Requests future opinion, not current preserved Phillips response. Missing original portions remain missing.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-617: Fresh complete context: Wednesday February2,1842 for February7ballot. Asks Royle vote and friends support Erasmus Athenaeum candidacy. Later successful election in Emma letter is future, not current outcome or Darwin Philosophical Club invitation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1361: Fresh complete extra source record: text is numbered council minute209 from October7,1850; catalogued after7October as proxy for missing secretary letter. Resolution instructs secretary to ask whether Darwin agrees to publication in parts. Minute content is institutional record, not delivered wording, with letter date/receipt unknown.1363is editorially identified reply to missing Lankester letter. Do not mark minute as source-complete Q or use nominal1851publication as proof actual appearance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1366A: Fresh complete extra source record: council minute216 from November4,1850; catalogue bounds November4–6 reflect inferred missing letter before November7reply. Minute reports Darwin letter read, identifiable as1364, and instructs secretary to request specimen plate for estimate. This supports institutional consideration, not full delivered secretary text or exact Darwin receipt. Editorial summary names James de Carle Sowerby, whereas1364 explicitly requests GB Sowerby junior; do not merge people or silently assign different engraver. Preserve response witness outside conversation graph.

visual_readings.visual_observation: Sloping section with upper removed slate indicated by dashed lines and label Slate denuded since boulders were dispersed; blocks of slate sit high at right over Carb. Limestone or anything, lower inclined band labelled Slate or Red conglomerate etc., basal Anything. It illustrates the denudation alternative in P2 that Darwin disputes, not observed proof of his coast-ice theory. Preserve spatial relationships and labels with source; a modern description is not original incoming prose.
